result.title: Energy-Based Reasoners: Your Recurrent Reasoner Should Be an Energy-Based Model
result.summary: Looping is a powerful inductive bias for reasoning. By repeatedly iterating a recurrent block, looped models can scale their effective depth and enable multi-step reasoning in latent space. However, existing looped models are not inherently guided by an explicit measure of progress, making it difficult to determine when to stop looping and how to improve upon the current state. To enable this, we introduce Energy-Based Reasoners (EBRs), which learn an energy function over latent reasoning states and formulate looped updates as gradient descent on this energy. The energy scores latent states, while its gradient guides refinement and provides a signal for stopping. To train EBRs effectively, we further introduce exploration-based training to discover additional modes and to better shape the energy landscape over a broader set of states. Across four algorithmic reasoning benchmarks, EBRs match or outperform prior recurrent reasoning models, achieving 99.9% accuracy on Sudoku-Extreme while using 345$\times$ less inference compute than the next-best model and maintaining comparable training compute. On all multi-solution benchmarks, EBRs achieve state-of-the-art coverage of distinct valid solutions while maintaining near-100% single-sample accuracy. These results suggest that energy-based models are a promising approach for strong reasoning performance.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 Energy-Based Reasoners，在循环块的 latent 推理状态上学习能量函数，把循环更新视为对该能量的梯度下降，使能量及其梯度同时用于状态精修与停止判断，并引入基于探索的训练以发现更多模态、塑造能量地形；在四个算法推理基准上匹配或超过已有循环推理模型，Sudoku-Extreme 达 99.9% 且推理算力大幅减少。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应 LVR 的生成与停止问题：用能量为 latent 状态提供进展度量与 STOP 信号，其多解覆盖结果与探索式训练可供核查 latent 迭代的收益成本权衡及轨迹监督方式。
